title: Integral local models on one pro-etale member
statement: For a scheme morphism g : S ⟶ X, an integral module M on X and a pro-etale object U over S, the point-model predicate for the pullback to U is equivalent to the existence of a finitely presented PbcIntegralRing module whose normalized integral section realization, pulled back along g and restricted to U, is isomorphic to the corresponding constant realization. This is one member and has no cover, stratification or Noetherian hypotheses.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3), one-member coefficient comparison in step 7.

proof.text: Use continuousScalarFinitePresentation to express the finitely presented point module as continuous scalar extension of an ordinary finitely presented valuation-ring module. Restrict scalars across ULift.down to obtain a PbcIntegralRing module. Finite presentation transfers across a ring equivalence: its algebra linear map is a linear equivalence, so the scalar ring is a finitely presented module of rank one over the target ring; transitivity of finite presentation along the scalar tower then applies to the module.

The point-pullback compositor identifies the pullback of the global point model with the point model over U.left. Compose the given point-model isomorphism with the scalar classification isomorphism and the inverse compositor. Transport this local isomorphism by integralSectionLocalIsomorphisms, then apply inverse image and slice restriction to the scalar-model comparison integralSectionScalarModels at the finitely presented scalar module. This gives the required completed constant realization on U.

Conversely transport the given PbcIntegralRing module across the inverse ULift ring equivalence. Transfer finite presentation as above. Compose the local constant-model isomorphism with the scalar equivalence counit and the inverse scalar-model comparison. Reflect this local isomorphism using integralSectionLocalIsomorphisms, and compose with the point-pullback compositor. The continuous scalar extension is finitely presented by the reverse implication of continuousScalarFinitePresentation. These constructions include empty presentations, torsion modules and empty schemes.

proof_origin.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); use the already proved continuous scalar finite-presentation classification and assemble the scalar-realization and localized-isomorphism comparisons. T6: genuine decomposition of the coefficient comparison; the original theorem has a complete Lean proof from these parts.

theorem integralSectionMemberModels (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (g : S ⟶ X) (U : S.ProEt)
    (M : AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) :
    sectionPointModelAlong (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) g M U.hom ↔
      integralSectionMemberModel l E g U M
